claims.text: Closed-loop in-situ laser power modulation can improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Closed-loop in-situ laser power modulation can improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Closed-loop in-situ laser power modulation can reduce fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Conventional static laser-power control produces nonuniform thermal gradients in high-entropy-alloy components.
Conventional static laser-power control produces residual stresses in high-entropy-alloy components.
Conventionally fabricated high-entropy-alloy components contain microstructural defects.
Nonuniform thermal gradients, residual stresses, and microstructural defects cause dimensional imprecision.
Nonuniform thermal gradients, residual stresses, and microstructural defects compromise mechanical properties.
The proposed feedback system dynamically adjusts laser power using real-time measurements of melt-pool characteristics.
Feedback-controlled laser modulation produces more uniform thermal gradients.
Feedback-controlled laser modulation improves control of melt-pool dynamics.
More uniform thermal gradients and controlled melt-pool dynamics promote homogeneous solidification.
More uniform thermal gradients and controlled melt-pool dynamics refine the microstructure.
Dynamic laser-power adjustment minimizes local overheating.
Dynamic laser-power adjustment minimizes local underheating.
Maintaining optimal melt-pool thermal conditions reduces residual stresses.
Maintaining optimal melt-pool thermal conditions reduces porosity and other defects.
The feedback-controlled process will improve yield strength and tensile strength relative to static laser parameters.
Effective feedback control requires sensor resolution and response rate sufficient to capture transient melt-pool behavior.
Nonlinear high-entropy-alloy melting behavior may overwhelm the feedback-control system.
